structural: The only structural obligation in the text is the prescribed signature: `impl<D: Domain> ValidationContext<'_, D> where D::Error: From<SourceError>` with `pub fn read_source(&self, item: &OutlineData) -> Result<D::NodeContent, D::Error>`. A declaration with a different receiver, bound or return type would not satisfy the text. The root `crates/trust-but-verify/src/procedure.rs#impl[ValidationContext<'_, D>]/fn[read_source]` declares exactly that. Its impl block has the `D::Error: From<crate::sources::SourceError>` bound.

The body does what the text describes. It resolves the item to a graph node with `self.graph.source_node(item)?` (`crates/trust-but-verify/src/domain.rs#trait[Domain]/fn[source_node]`). It then interns the node with `ValidationCache::intern_source` and reads it with `self.read`. `read` is `impl[ValidationContext<'d, D>]#2/fn[read]` in `procedure.rs`. It goes through `read_snapshot`, which is reached from the marked root, so it needs no marker of its own.

I did not read `read_snapshot`. The observation recording that `read_source.inputs` describes is delegated to it and is behavioral. It depends on which node and fingerprint get recorded, not on how the code is structured, so tests cover it. The `read_source.inputs` text, which the subject only cites, adds no further structural obligation, because every clause in it specifies observable behavior. No other root is needed.

behavioral: The subject's behavioral obligations are covered by `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/project_sources.rs#mod[tests]/fn[direct_source_reads_preserve_mapping_errors_and_record_only_successful_returns]`.

- **Resolve the item to its graph node.** The test reads `source.txt` and asserts that the read goes to `source-node`. It asserts this through `read_nodes == ["source-node", "source-node"]`.
- **Mapping failures.** Two unsupported addresses are tried: an unknown file (`unknown.txt`) and an unknown selector (`line[unknown]`). Each must return an error containing "unsupported source item". Each must leave `dependencies()` empty. The test also asserts that no domain read occurred (`reads == 0`, `read_nodes` empty). The `From<SourceError>` conversion is therefore exercised and preserved.
- **Read the contents and return them.** After the failure is cleared, the successful read returns "prepared contents", checked with `returned.format()`.
- **Read failures record nothing.** With `fail_read` set, the error "prepared source read failed" is propagated. `dependencies()` stays empty, which matches "Failures record no successful observation" in the cited `requirements.sdk.graph.validation-context.read_source.inputs`.
- **Record the observation on success.** `dependencies()` must equal exactly `[Dependency::Node(source-node, returned.fingerprint())]`. This checks the node identity and the fingerprint of the supplied contents. The failed read left no entry, so only the successful return was recorded.
- **Staleness.** The record produced by `finish` is current. After the contents change, it is no longer current. This covers "stale when that node's fingerprint changes".

The cited `read_source.inputs` also covers agent reads and the standalone outline parser. Those are not obligations of this subject's direct method, so they need no test here. `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/public_api.rs#fn[public_exports_match_the_appendix]` only checks the exported API surface. It does not test behavior of this requirement.

I found no unresolved ambiguity and no missing scenario.

text: Resolve an outline item to its graph node, read the contents, and record the observation under {cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.validation-context.read_source.inputs`.
impl<D: Domain> ValidationContext<'_, D> where D::Error: From<SourceError> {
A successful source read records the mapped node's identity and the fingerprint
record when returning the contents; agent reads record when delivering them.
The dependency becomes stale when that node's fingerprint changes. The source
mapping cannot return an untracked successful read. Calling the standalone
outline parser directly records no graph dependency; a tracked node read must
enclose its use when its contents contribute to an assessment.
